provenance.source: Figtree variable font, Google Fonts repository github.com/google/fonts, path ofl/figtree
Vector adaptive icon authored in this build (ajrakh star, resist white on madder #C7372F); no raster assets

display-large.purpose: Screen statements: Are you okay?; countdown overrides to 72/76sp.

display-small.purpose: Set up Saathi, My trips, Your contacts were told.

headline-medium.purpose: Reversed-plate labels: Hold for help, I'm okay.

headline-small.purpose: Don't get in; second spoken phrase.

title-large.purpose: Sheet heads, minutes watched, quiet help-plate label.

title-small.purpose: Station names, tile labels, banner heads.

body-large.purpose: Explanations under screen statements, in fg2.

motion.name: stamp
motion.value: CubicBezierEasing(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1); scale 1.6 to 1 over 200ms, alpha 0.35 to 1 over 260ms
motion.purpose: Each watched minute stamps the next ajrakh star. Skipped when animator duration scale is 0.

motion.name: hold-fill
motion.purpose: Hold for help fills with a 22% black wash; completion raises the alert.

motion.name: countdown
motion.value: 100ms tick, alum arc sweeping from -90 degrees
motion.purpose: Check-in ring drains over a 10s window.

motion.name: count-turnover
motion.value: in: vertical slide 220ms on the stamp curve + fade 160ms; out: slide 160ms + fade 120ms
motion.purpose: The readiness count turns over like a departures board when a protection changes. Skipped under Remove animations.

motion.name: shared-axis-page
motion.value: in: slide 1/5 width 260ms on the stamp curve + fade 220ms; out: slide 200ms + fade 120ms
motion.purpose: Settings list to sub-page and back; a page enters from the end, the list returns from the start. Skipped under Remove animations.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.value: single column; verified at 1080x2400 and at 130% font scale

components.name: Hold for help plate

components.name: Quiet help plate (during alert)

components.name: Star thread
components.description: Stamped ajrakh stars on a star-off rail; the newest turns alum on a stall.
components.css: .ds-thread { display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 5px; padding: 6px 6px; background: linear-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,0.14),rgba(255,255,255,0.14)) center/2px 100% no-repeat, #0D1222; } .ds-star { width: 14px; height: 14px; fill: #EEF0F7; animation: ds-stamp 0.26s cubic-bezier(0.05,0.7,0.1,1) both; } .ds-star-stall { fill: #E7B94A; } @keyframes ds-stamp { from { transform: scale(1.6); opacity: 0.35; } to { transform: scale(1); opacity: 1; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-star { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Saathi is dyed like Ajrakh cloth. Night is indigo ground and day is resist white. Madder red is the costly dye, so it goes only on help and alerts. Alum gold is the mordant, the attention colour that shows before anything is sent. The one motif is the eight-point ajrakh star, two squares with one turned 45 degrees. It appears as the app mark, and it is also the trip thread: one star is stamped onto her route for each minute Saathi watches. When the trip stalls, the newest star turns alum and the stamping stops.

Screens follow a map-and-sheet trip layout like Pixel and Maps. A calm, luminance-only map sits at the top, and a 28dp sheet carries the line diagram. Help is pinned below the scroll so it never leaves her thumb. Density is low and controls are large: every target is at least 48dp and the help row is at least 140dp. Each screen has exactly one full-contrast "reversed plate", the thing to press. Depth comes from tonal steps and hairlines, never from shadows.

Native Android: Jetpack Compose with Material 3 roles. Every colour above maps onto an M3 slot or onto the `SaathiColors` extension in `ui/theme/SaathiTheme.kt`, which is the normative source.
keyCharacteristics: Indigo night ground with three tonal surface steps, and a resist-white day ground with white surfaces.
Madder reserved for help and alerts. Alum for stalls, check-ins and pre-send attention.
Eight-point ajrakh star as both the mark and the trip thread, stamped one per watched minute.
One reversed plate per screen: Hold for help normally, I'm okay during an alert or check-in.
Figtree in one family at weights 400 to 700, with system Noto for Kannada and Devanagari.
Flat and tonal throughout, with 1dp hairlines instead of boxes or shadows.

rules.name: The Madder Rule
rules.body: Madder red is spent only on help and alerts: the help plate, alert confirmations, a plate mismatch, and the "something happened / don't get in" escalations. Nothing decorative is red, and nothing turns red before an alert is actually sent.

rules.name: The Alum-Before-Send Rule
rules.body: Attention before anything is sent is alum: stalls, the check-in pill, and the draining countdown ring. Alum turns to madder only once contacts have been told.

rules.name: The Ink-3-Is-Not-Text Rule
rules.body: fg3 colours marks and never text. Secondary text uses fg2.

rules.name: The Tight-At-Size Rule
rules.body: Negative tracking applies only from titleMedium up. Body and label styles stay at 0.

rules.name: The Grow-Don't-Clip Rule
rules.body: Layouts that hold text grow with the system font scale (`heightIn(min)` with `IntrinsicSize.Min`) instead of clipping. The help row was verified at 130% font scale.

rules.name: The Pinned Help Rule
rules.body: Help never scrolls away. The help row lives outside the scroll container, under a hair rule, on every trip state.

rules.name: The One Plate Chip Rule
rules.body: On a trip the vehicle plate outranks the city. While a plate chip shows in the map chip row, the city chip is hidden.

rules.name: The Tonal-Only Rule
rules.body: Separate layers by surface step or hairline. If something needs to read as "above", move it one surface step up rather than adding a shadow.

rules.name: The Required-Versus-Optional Rule
rules.body: Alum marks only a required protection that is missing (people to text, her name, the permissions Saathi runs on). An optional one she has not set, or an Off she chose, gets a quiet ring and a fg2 summary: never alum, never a "Fix", never madder. Leaving an optional protection off is her choice, not a fault.

dos: Do read every colour through `MaterialTheme.colorScheme` or `Saathi.colors`, so both night and day resolve.
Do keep exactly one reversed plate per screen: Hold for help normally, I'm okay during an alert or check-in.
Do step the help plate back to helpContainer with "Hold to alert again" while an alert is active.
Do pin help outside the scroll, under a 1dp hair rule.
Do stamp one ajrakh star per watched minute, and turn the newest one alum when the trip stalls.
Do use alum for anything that asks for attention before a message is sent.
Do let containers grow with font scale (`heightIn(min)` with intrinsic height) rather than clip names.
Do use the indigo tile for the in-app mark, and keep the madder launcher icon.
Do mark a ready protection with an indigo star, a missing required one with an alum ring, and an unset optional one with a quiet ring (ink-3 by night, ink-2 by day).
Do make each settings row one whole button with a stateDescription, and divide rows with hairlines.
Do skip the stamp, the count turnover and the page slide when Remove animations is on.
donts: Don't use madder for anything other than help and alerts. That includes validation errors and decoration.
Don't turn a countdown or stall red before an alert is actually sent.
Don't set text in fg3. It colours marks only.
Don't show the city chip while a plate chip is showing.
Don't add shadows. Separate layers with a surface step or a hairline.
Don't put a second full-contrast plate on a screen that already has one.
Don't mark an optional protection, or an Off she chose, in alum or with "Fix".
Don't box settings rows in cards. The readiness plate is the only container on the Settings list.
